status: version 10. Versions 1 to 4 were approved by the owner. Since 7 Oct 2026 a field is added by the rules when it passes the four tests, and the digest of the run that added it says so. The game reads this file.
about: Every field a thing may carry, and the only values that field may take. A field that does not apply to a thing is left out of that thing; it is never written as 'not applicable'. The wording is what a child sees or hears; it is not data.
rules: A field holds the everyday meaning, which is what the game sorts by.
An _academic field is added only where science disagrees with the everyday meaning. It never sorts a board and never marks a child wrong.

A new field enters this file in one of two ways, and the version number then goes up by one. Up to version 4 the owner approved each field and its values. Since 7 Oct 2026 the job adds a field when it passes four tests: every value has at least four familiar things; every thing it applies to has exactly one value, by two checks that agree; sample boards have one clean solution; and it is not an existing field in other words. Such a field says who added it.
A thing that truly fits more than one value of a field lists them all, and stays off boards sorted by that field.
The value 'depends' is only for things experts debate. It needs a note saying why, and such a thing also stays off boards sorted by that field.

An _academic field marked `only_where_science_differs` is carried only by the things for which a scientist's answer differs from the everyday one. It is absent everywhere else, and it never sorts a board.
A field marked `withdrawn` was taken back by the owner. It is kept, with the values things carry for it, and never sorts a board.

Since the owner's second ruling of 7 Oct 2026 a new field is a question from the field library (tools/content/field_library.json), which holds real ways of sorting from biology, geography and everyday life; such a field names its library question. A field may have more than four values, and a board uses any four of them that have enough familiar things.
